title: Discrete time at the Big Bang: one Planck step of Reeb flow
html:
Remark. Discrete time at the Big Bang: one Planck step of Reeb flow

We discretize the continuous Reeb flow \phi_t^q (q-Reeb flow) at the Big Bang. Here the substrate parameter q \to \infty and the quantum Planck constant \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} \to 1 (quantum Planck constant). This limits defines a Planck step—the minimal dynamical time unit of the QOU. Time is discrete at the origin.

Algebraic normalization. The q-deformed Reeb flow rotates the affine coordinate Z of a state (substrate radial coordinate):

  \mathcal{L}_\xi Z = J\hbar_q Z.

The naive period of this rotation is T = 2\pi/\hbar_q. The transcendental factor 2\pi obstructs finite-field and p-adic realisations (finite field realisation, Witt vector lift). To resolve this, we define one full Reeb circuit as one unit of time:

  t_P(q)  :=  \frac{1}{\hbar_q}
  =  \frac{1}{1 - q^{-1}}
  =  \frac{q}{q - 1}.

Because t_P(q) is a rational function, it is well-defined over any field k where q \neq 1.

  • Over \mathbb{F}_\pp: t_P = q/(q-1) \in \mathbb{F}_\pp for q \in \mathbb{F}_\pp^\times \setminus \{1\}.
  • Over \mathbb{Q}_\pp: t_P \in \mathbb{Q}_\pp. Its \pp-adic valuation v_\pp(t_P) = v_\pp(q) - v_\pp(q-1) encodes proximity to the classical limit.
  • Over \mathbb{C}: It reproduces the angular period up to 2\pi.

The Planck step acts as the polynomial iteration f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) (Julia set of Reeb flow).

Limits.

Regime q \hbar_q t_P Interpretation
Big Bang q \to \infty \to 1 \to 1 Minimal step; time is fastest
Physical q = q_0 (local substrate q) 0.0988 \approx 10.1 Our Planck time
Classical q \to 1 \to 0 \to \infty No Reeb period; time freezes

At the Big Bang, t_P \to 1. One Planck step exactly equals one unit. The continuous Reeb flow is merely the \mathbb{R}-shadow of this discrete iteration. There is no sub-step resolution.

One Planck length of flow. After one Planck step, the Reeb flow displaces a state by exactly one Planck length:

  \ell_P(q)
  =  \hbar_q \cdot t_P
  =  (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \frac{q}{q-1}
  =  1.

This is the normalised total --- one full Reeb circuit, an angular displacement carrying no length scale --- and it evaluates to 1 over any field precisely because \hbar_q is its per-step share (see share versus total). It is not the same object as the local \ell_P^{\mathrm{step}} \sim \hbar_q of the Planck information unit. The angular velocity \hbar_q changes with q. At the Big Bang, the fiber is traversed at maximum speed (\hbar_q = 1). Near heat death, the rotation halts.

Discrete time at the Big Bang. The Big Bang initial state (bundle initial conditions) is a formal sum \mathcal{S}_0 = \sum_i (p_i, H_i). It specifies fiber data without horizontal transport. The first Planck step \phi_1^q applies horizontal transport for the first time. It connects neighboring fibers, initiates the q-connection, and begins information propagation across the brane.

Before the first step, position is known exactly but momentum is entirely undetermined. After one step, the q-connection \nabla_q correlates adjacent fibers. It produces the first non-trivial holonomy. The Heisenberg commutator [\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q = J\hbar_q \approx J is near-maximal. The first tick of time maximizes uncertainty.

Over \mathbb{F}_\pp, this first step evaluates f_q once: z_1 = z_0^2 + c(q). The first moment after the Big Bang is a single polynomial evaluation.

Counting Planck steps. The count of Planck steps measures dynamical distance in Reeb time. From the Big Bang (q_0 \gg 1) to our universe (q = q_0):

  N(q_0, q)
  =  \int_{q}^{q_0}
  \frac{dq'}{t_P(q')\dot{q}(q')}

where \dot{q} is the coordinate time derivative of the substrate parameter. Over \mathbb{F}_\pp, the integral becomes a finite sum.

Information per step. Each Planck step propagates information across one fiber. The information content per step is bounded by the Julia-set Hausdorff dimension d_H(q) (Julia set of Reeb flow) over \mathbb{C}, or by the orbit complexity of f_q over \mathbb{F}_\pp. At the Big Bang, the dynamics is simplest and each step carries minimal information. As q approaches the golden threshold, the complexity peaks. The universe processes information faster as it cools, reaching peak capacity near the golden ratio.

Relation to 't Hooft's ontological CA. 't Hooft [thooft2016] posits a Planck-scale tick as the elementary time unit of a deterministic cellular automaton. The Planck step t_P(q) = q/(q-1) realizes this tick. It is algebraically derived from the substrate parameter q rather than posited independently. It recovers the dimensional Planck time via the archimedean realisation at q_0.
